memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If a man has sexual relations with his daughter-in-law, both of them are to be put to death. What they have done is a perversion; their blood will be on their own heads. If a man has sexual relations with a man as one does with a woman, both of them have done what is detestable. They are to be put to death; their blood will be on their own heads.'" - Lev 20:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses correspond to prohibitions we met in chapter 18, now with penalties attached.

On the first: God is again protecting the household. A daughter-in-law entering a family was vulnerable — dependent, often young, with limited power. God draws a line around her.

On the second: this reflects the same understanding of God's design that runs from Genesis 2 through to Jesus' own words about marriage in Matthew 19 — man and woman, joined as one flesh. That has been the consistent teaching of the Christian church across every tradition and century, and it remains the position of Scripture.

But how we hold this matters as much as what we hold, and three things need saying plainly.

The penalty here belonged to Israel's civil law. It has never been given to the church, and any Christian who reads this as licence for hostility has read it against Christ.

This sin is not ranked above others. Paul's lists place sexual sin alongside greed, gossip and pride, and then say to the church: and that is what some of you were. But you were washed (1 Cor 6:11).

And some who read this are believers who experience same-sex attraction and are seeking to follow Christ at real cost. If that is you: you are a brother or sister, and the church needs you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you hold Scripture's teaching with conviction and humility together?
2. Have you treated some sins as beyond grace in ways Scripture does not?
3. Is your church a place where anyone can be honest and still be loved?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me hold Your Word faithfully and hold people gently, never using one against the other. Thank You that all of us come to Christ needing washing. Amen.
